ENTER_PAIR_NUMBERS: Enter pair numbers (1-40) separated by commas or spaces
AT_BOND_DESC: Two hydrogen bonds. Stability: medium. This complementary pairing is fundamental to DNA replication and transcription processes.
GC_BOND_DESC: Three hydrogen bonds. Stability: high. The stronger bonds make G-C pairs more resistant to denaturation and crucial for genome stability.
LANGUAGE_HINT: Select interface language for comfortable work
DNA_DESCRIPTION: DNA (deoxyribonucleic acid) is a molecule that contains the genetic information of all living organisms. It consists of two helices connected by nucleotide pairs: adenine-thymine (A-T) and guanine-cytosine (G-C).
PAIR_FACT_1: This is the very first pair in our DNA model. A-T pairs make up about 58% of all nucleotide pairs in the human genome.
PAIR_FACT_2: G-C pair! Guanine and cytosine form the most stable bond among nucleotides thanks to three hydrogen bonds.
PAIR_FACT_3: A-T pair. Interestingly, in some viral DNA, the A-T pair ratio can reach 75%!
PAIR_FACT_4: G-C pair. In the human genome, G-C pairs make up about 42% of all nucleotide pairs.
PAIR_FACT_5: A-T pair. Thymine differs from uracil (found in RNA) only by a methyl group.
PAIR_FACT_6: G-C pair. Cytosine can spontaneously turn into uracil, which is one of the causes of mutations.
PAIR_FACT_7: A-T pair. Adenine is one of the most common nucleotides in nature.
PAIR_FACT_8: G-C pair. Guanine was discovered in 1844, earlier than other nucleotide bases.
PAIR_FACT_9: A-T pair. In DNA of some bacteria, A-T pair content can exceed 70%.
PAIR_FACT_10: G-C pair. Cytosine plays a key role in gene expression regulation through methylation.
PAIR_FACT_11: A-T pair. This pair participates in forming DNA replication start points.
PAIR_FACT_12: G-C pair. G-C pairs are more common in gene promoter regions.
PAIR_FACT_13: A-T pair. Thymine absorbs UV radiation and can form dimers, causing mutations.
PAIR_FACT_14: G-C pair. Cytosine is the basis for synthesizing important coenzymes in the cell.
PAIR_FACT_15: A-T pair. In some organisms, A-T pairs serve as markers for transcription regulation.
PAIR_FACT_16: G-C pair. Guanine participates in GTP formation - an important energy source.
PAIR_FACT_17: A-T pair. Adenosine is part of ATP - the universal energy source for cells.
PAIR_FACT_18: G-C pair. Cytosine can be modified into 5-methylcytosine, affecting gene expression.
PAIR_FACT_19: A-T pair. This pair is often found in non-coding regions of the genome.
PAIR_FACT_20: G-C pair. G-C pairs are more resistant to heat than A-T pairs.
PAIR_FACT_21: A-T pair. Thymine replaced uracil in DNA to increase molecular stability.
PAIR_FACT_22: G-C pair. Cytosine participates in pseudouridine formation in RNA.
PAIR_FACT_23: A-T pair. Adenosine is a precursor for many coenzyme syntheses.
PAIR_FACT_24: G-C pair. Guanine forms guanine quartets in some DNA structures.
PAIR_FACT_25: A-T pair. This pair is often used as a marker in molecular biology.
PAIR_FACT_26: G-C pair. Cytosine can be hydrolyzed to uracil by acids.
PAIR_FACT_27: A-T pair. Thymine was discovered in 1901 from bovine thymus gland.
PAIR_FACT_28: G-C pair. G-C pairs form the basis of telomeres - chromosome ends.
PAIR_FACT_29: A-T pair. Adenosine participates in sleep-wake regulation through the adenosinergic system.
PAIR_FACT_30: G-C pair. Cytosine is one of the rarest nucleotides in some viral genomes.
PAIR_FACT_31: A-T pair. This pair plays an important role in DNA-protein complex formation.
PAIR_FACT_32: G-C pair. Guanine can form tetrahedral structures in some molecules.
PAIR_FACT_33: A-T pair. Thymine absorbs UV-range light, protecting DNA from damage.
PAIR_FACT_34: G-C pair. Cytosine participates in forming rare nucleotides like pseudo-isocytosine.
PAIR_FACT_35: A-T pair. Adenosine is the basis for caffeine and theobromine synthesis.
PAIR_FACT_36: G-C pair. G-C pairs bind more effectively to some antibiotics.
PAIR_FACT_37: A-T pair. This pair is often found in chromosome centromeres.
PAIR_FACT_38: G-C pair. Cytosine can be demethylated by TET enzymes to activate genes.
PAIR_FACT_39: A-T pair. Thymine has a higher melting temperature in DNA composition.
PAIR_FACT_40: G-C pair. The last pair in our model. G-C pairs determine transcription direction in many genes.
